why: Three product defects were found by a person on 2026-08-16 (findings 049, 050, and the unbound Ctrl+C) and none of them was reachable by any automated round, because every harness calls the shell directly and none of them went through the product page's own handlers. They were found one at a time, by walking into them. This file turns that into a rule with the same shape as the shell bundle's: every handler and every toolbar action the product page has must be either DRIVEN by a named harness or WAIVED with a reason, and anything else fails the audit. What is uncovered here is where the next one of those defects is.
rule: paths(page) - driven - waived must be empty

driven.how: a synthesised PointerEvent on #canvas, through the page's own handler; placeCaret is confirmed by the engine
the drag that precedes the copy check
ends every click and every drag
a ClipboardEvent on #sink; the check classifies the outcome by which error the clipboard adapter raises
the toolbar's delegated click handler, via a real button.click()
the product's own save button; the bytes are captured through a declared URL.createObjectURL shim and must BE an ODT
the default --action of the smoke run; the revision must advance by exactly one

text is typed into the product's own #text field and the product's own button is pressed; the revision must advance by exactly one AND the text must be in the ODT the product then saves. Mutation `insert-text` reads el.text.placeholder instead of el.text.value -- finding 049's shape on this path -- and the check must go red.

pressed straight after the insert above; the marker text must be GONE from the saved ODT, read from the document rather than from the revision counter, because D1 covers undo through the shell and this is the button. Mutations `undo` (does nothing) and `undo-twice` (takes back one edit too many) must each turn it red.

the product's own recovery button, pressed in the state the product OFFERS it in -- reached through the page's own buttons: click past the end of a line, insert-paragraph-break, then a list action on the new empty paragraph (finding 046's cell). The oracle is that the notice is shown and enabled, that pressing it returns the session to ready, and that the product can save a real ODT afterwards. Mutation `rollback` (wired to undo instead) is detected; mutation `toolbar-drops-the-list-action` proves the NOT_ESTABLISHED branch cannot hide a broken toolbar.

pressed to create the empty paragraph the recovery route needs; not separately asserted, so it is driven rather than verified -- if it stopped working the recovery route would go red, which is a real if indirect signal.

a File synthesised from a fixture's bytes is assigned to #file and a change event dispatched, through the page's own handler. The oracle is the document the ENGINE ends up holding -- the run saves afterwards and requires text that exists only in the handed-over file, and none from the fixture that was open before. Mutation `open-file` re-opens the fixture while still updating the filename, and is detected.

a synthesised InputEvent('beforeinput', {inputType: deleteContentBackward}) on #sink; the oracle is that the page cancels it AND the revision advances, i.e. it reached the engine. The input adapter also listens for beforeinput but drops both delete types as `ignored-input-type` without preventing them, which is why this is not a second handler for the same work -- checked before it was written, after the paste episode.

a synthesised KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key: ArrowLeft}) on #sink; the oracle is the page cancelling it and the status line reporting a dispatched caret move. LIMIT, stated because this audit works per LISTENER and cannot see inside one: the same handler also carries Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+S, and neither is exercised. So `driven` here means the handler is reached, not that every branch in it is. Ctrl+Z's own coverage is the undo check, which presses the button rather than the key.

a synthesised ClipboardEvent('cut') on #sink; classified by which error the clipboard adapter raises, exactly like the copy check. The removal half is NOT established: the delete runs only after a successful clipboard write and WebDriver refuses that.

uncovered.risk: MEDIUM -- opening a second document in one page. The session disposes its engine on close, so this is also the only product path that comes near the search-after-reopen wedge.
LOW -- covered through the shell by D1; the button itself is untested.
LOW -- endDrag(null); reachable when the browser takes the pointer away.

LOW -- one line that forwards a click to #file.click(). Not driven because clicking it opens the OS file chooser, which no driver here can operate and which would block the browser. The handler it forwards to IS driven (listener:change#file), so what is unproven is the forwarding itself, not the opening. Same class of gap as D5's trusted-input requirement: it needs a human, not a better harness.

LOW -- dispatches enabled:false to all four inline formats. Not driven because finding 059 has every one of those failing with LOK_COMMAND_FAILED on the shipped artifact, so a check here would measure that defect rather than this button.
